title: Ukraine says it hit Russian petrochemical complex in Tatarstan, 1,000 km from the front
dek: Ukraine's General Staff said drones struck the Nizhnekamskneftekhim complex and a neighbouring refinery unit, and a helicopter-parts plant in Bryansk. Russia said it downed 533 drones; local officials reported six people wounded in Nizhnekamsk.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Ukraine's armed forces said they struck one of Russia's largest petrochemical complexes, in Nizhnekamsk in the Republic of Tatarstan, and a neighbouring oil refinery overnight into Sunday. The General Staff said in a statement that it also hit a plant making helicopter parts in Russia's Bryansk region.

Russia's defence ministry said its air defences destroyed 533 Ukrainian drones overnight over more than a dozen regions and annexed Crimea, according to reports. The mayor of Nizhnekamsk described a "massive and prolonged attack by enemy drones" that wounded six people and damaged a residential building, the reports said. Neither side's account of the damage could be independently verified.

## What Ukraine says it hit

The General Staff said explosions were heard at Nizhnekamskneftekhim, a petrochemical complex that belongs to the Russian group Sibur, followed by a fire. It said a fire also broke out at the ELOU-AVT-7 unit of the nearby TAIF-NK refinery, which it described as the refinery's only primary crude-processing unit of its type. Nizhnekamsk is more than 1,000 km from the front line.

The General Staff said the complex makes synthetic rubber used in military vehicle and aircraft tyres, and that some types serve as binders in the solid fuel of Iskander ballistic missiles. "Every period of downtime at such plants reduces Russia's military capabilities," it said, adding that Ukraine was acting in self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter. The extent of the damage at both sites was still being assessed, it said.

It also reported a strike on the Monolit plant in Trubchevsk, in Bryansk region, which it said makes helicopters, spare parts and components. Ukraine also claimed that an airfield at Akhtubinsk in Astrakhan region and a drone launch site in Oryol region were hit, according to reports.

## Russian strikes and casualties

Russian and Russian-installed officials reported three people killed elsewhere, one in Taganrog and two in the occupied part of Ukraine's Luhansk region, according to reports. In Ukraine, the air force said it neutralised 106 of the drones Russia launched overnight. Russian strikes caused power cuts in the Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa regions and damaged a dormitory in Zaporizhzhia, according to Ukrainian officials quoted in reports.

## Background

Ukraine has spent much of this year attacking Russian refineries, oil terminals and chemical plants with long-range drones, describing them as legitimate targets that fund and supply Russia's war effort. Russia, in turn, has kept up attacks on Ukraine's power grid as winter approaches.

The strikes come as US envoys press both sides towards a settlement. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that US negotiators had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas region in return for NATO membership, and that he would not take such a decision alone. US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are due to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, which takes place on 18 and 19 November.

## Why it matters for India

India is one of the largest buyers of Russian crude oil, and attacks on Russian refining and export infrastructure can shift the volumes and discounts available to Indian refiners. New Delhi has called repeatedly for an end to the war through dialogue and diplomacy, and has kept up trade and defence ties with Moscow while expanding them with Western partners.
